query: Write the analysis plan for our test of a simplified signup form. Signups per day: about 6,000, all eligible. Primary metric: activation_rate (trusted in our registry, baseline 12%, unit user). Our prior store is at priors.jsonl. The PM will definitely watch the dashboard daily.
expected_behavior: Produces a complete pre-registration: user as randomisation unit with an explicit interference call (none, single-player surface), an MDE anchored to the prior store (effects of 0.05 to 0.4pp, sized via gallop.power or size_test.py rather than asserted), a defined exposure event fired in both arms, guardrails attached up front, exactly one pre-registered segment, a numeric decision rule written before launch, and, because the PM will peek daily, a sequential/always-valid design declared now rather than a fixed-horizon test. Without the skill, the plan typically omits the exposure event and the peeking policy and states the MDE as a wish.
